Concerns about AI’s role in legal practice remain widespread, particularly when its outputs influence legal analysis or client outcomes. external.description: Google has moved AI Mode from travel advice into hotel checkout. If you plan trips through Search, the booking fight is now happening inside the answer box. Google said on August 27 that AI Mode in Search can now track flight prices and show points and miles rates for flights and hotels. It can also complete some hotel bookings through Google Pay. ->Australian Broadcasting Corporation | More on "Bird flu threatens Antarctic wildlife sanctuary" at BigEarthData.ai | #Pandemic #Science #Island #BirdFlu

external.description: The Australian Antarctic Division will launch a mission to extract personnel from Macquarie Island in the Southern Ocean due to the psychological risk posed by a potential outbreak of bird flu. The sub-Antarctic island, 1,500 kilometres south-east of Hobart, is a World Heritage-listed wildlife sanctuary with up to 4 million seabirds and 100,000 seals. The island is currently free of the deadly H5 strain of bird flu. But once it arrives, up to 90 per cent of baby elephant seals could perish, as happened on Heard Island over summer, when 13,000 pups died from bird flu. The Australian government says exposing expeditioners to such harrowing scenes is untenable. "We've come to this really difficult decision of withdrawing staff," federal environment department deputy secretary Sean Sullivan told the ABC. "And that's being done primarily for the psychological risks that will be facing staff if they are there for extended periods of time inside a mass mortality event." Australia's research station on Macquarie Island is located within metres of a 2,500-strong colony of elephant seals. Mr Sullivan said it would be highly distressing for expeditioners to endure a prolonged wildlife mass mortality event on their doorstep in the event of an outbreak...

external.description:
So, I’ve been no fan of Gumroad for quite some time, and now they’ve gone even further all-in on using AI for everything and being especially gross about it.

Here’s some alternatives that are worth considering.

### Ko-Fi

It’s what I use for my main shop these days. Their pricing is quite nice: 5% cut for transactions on the free tier, 0% if you pay $12/month. They support both digital and physical goods, although their variant support and shipping calculation is a bit weak.

The main downside is that people don’t realize that Ko-Fi has a fully-fledged shop and membership system; for whatever reason everyone still just thinks of them as being a tip jar. Which is unfortunate, because they’re quite good at the other things too!

### Payhip

Payhip is similar to Ko-Fi, but does a better job of marketing themselves as a storefront. Their pricing is _okay_ although not as good as Ko-Fi’s; the free tier is a 5% cut, but it costs significantly more to pay down the cut ($29/month to get 2% and $99/month to get 0%).

I haven’t worked with them directly but a friend of mine speaks highly of it, and it seems like it was designed with inventory and variant support from the ground up although I don’t have any idea of how it actually works to the user. So I’ll probably sign up for it since some of my art pieces and coffee items that I’ve been meaning to list for sale again are pretty clumsy to list on Ko-Fi.

### itch.io

itch.io is mostly seen as a place to sell games and conduct game jams, but it’s also great for selling digital assets and music. They let you set your platform cut, and default to 10%.

There’s _technically_ support for physical merch although it’s quite weak, so I wouldn’t recommend it for that purpose.

### Jinxxy

Jinxxy is designed specifically for VR assets, and has become very popular for VRChat creators in particular. As far as I can tell they _only_ support VRChat assets, however. Similarly to itch.io they let you specify your own cut, and default to 5%.

### Patreon

I’m not exactly a fan of Patreon (despite having capitulated) but in addition to memberships they also have a means of selling digital goods. I don’t know anyone who really uses it that way and the discovery is pretty bad. It also only supports digital goods, and they charge a 10% cut unless you get one of the higher plans and I can’t really be bothered to research this one too much. But it’s an alternative to Gumroad so it was worth listing all the same.
external.title: Gumroad alternatives
